title: Discovery and Source Selection: Visual Guide
outline: Title: Discovery and Source Selection: Visual Guide

1. From Frontier To Leads | five discovery channels toggled on and off over ten real pages, showing which become reachable and the median detection lag | the frontier, politeness and canonicalization all start from a URL somebody had to discover, and link traversal alone leaves orphan, brand-new and unlinked pages invisible

2. Poll, Diff, Confirm | a sitemap poll with conditional-request and file-changed toggles, a slider for entries that vanished, the fetched status and a removal decision | a 304 skips 12 MB but proves nothing about the listed pages, 100,000 to 100,500 URLs is 500 new candidates, and absence from the file is never proof of deletion

3. Events Out Of Order | five at-least-once notification events for document d42 delivered one at a time under two sink policies | applying arrival order lets version 7 overwrite version 8 with no error logged, while accepting only a newer source version buys reordering tolerance and idempotence at once

4. Cost Per Unique Page | sliders over planned queries, pages per query and price per request, with a per-page table of unique discoveries and marginal cost | 1,000 queries x 5 pages at $0.005 is 5,000 calls and $25 for about 2,000 unique URLs — 1.25 cents each — and the marginal page is far dearer than the average

5. Seeds And Scope Gate | selectable seeds scored by the union of corpus regions and marginal contribution, then eight candidate URLs run through a scope policy with parameter and redirect rules | seeds decide what is reachable and scope decides what is allowed, so judge a seed by marginal coverage and re-evaluate scope after every redirect
